submission.name: Molecule Habit Garden
submission.tagline: Grow a routine by turning small goals into building blocks.
submission.inspiration: We wanted to make personal goals feel easier to start by connecting daily habits with a visual sense of progress. A second idea came from molecule tools that turn a compact text description into a possible sequence of components.
submission.what_it_does: The prototype lets users choose a goal, log a few daily tasks, and see a small progress garden change as they keep going. A separate mocked screen accepts a molecule-style string and displays a sample sequence of habit steps, but it is not connected to the goal tracker.
submission.how_we_built_it: We used React Native for the task and reflection screens, Express with Supabase for user progress, and a Cohere-powered coach concept for guidance. The molecule input borrows the compact-string-to-sequence idea, but the sequence generator is currently a mock and does not produce validated biochemical predictions.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: The quiz and task data were difficult to keep in sync with stored progress, and the screens for the two ideas remain separate. Public Wi-Fi also caused intermittent development connection problems.
submission.accomplishments: We made a usable task and reflection flow with levels stored in Supabase, and explored a separate interface for representing a sequence from a short string input.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned how much care it takes to keep progress data consistent across app screens. We also saw that converting a compact input into a meaningful sequence needs domain validation, not just a visual result.
submission.whats_next: We would connect the sequence idea to a clearly bounded, validated dataset or remove it from the habit flow. The app could also add user-created categories and voice reflections.
